pull.title: Detect transaction problems early during deserialization
pull.body:
This is split off from #36521 (and not included in #36895), as it's effectively an independent improvement.

This introduces a number of additional checks that are applied during transaction deserialization, which reduce various worst case deserialization time scenarios:
* Reject transactions with more txins or more txouts than can possibly fit in a block (applied always)
* Reject transactions with 0 txins or 0 txouts (applied in P2P code only; there are RPCs like `fundrawtransaction` that explicitly support transactions with 0 inputs)

This is a mild behavior change, as detecting these problems early causes them to be treated as deserialization errors, which in P2P logic cause messages to be ignored instead of peer disconnection.

events.message:
primitives: reject txs with more inputs or outputs than fit in a block

When deserializing a transaction, read the input and output counts
first, and fail before reading the inputs or outputs if more of them
are claimed than can fit in a block, given their minimum size (41 bytes
for an input, 9 for an output). Such a transaction can never be valid.

This allows us to allocate the vin and vout vectors immediately, rather
than sequentially in batches of 5 MB as the std::vector deserializer
does, because that memory becomes bounded: to 2.7 MB for 24390 inputs,
and 5.3 MB for 111111 outputs. It is a preparation for further changes
that rely on this structuring of conditionals.

This affects all places where transactions are deserialized. Through
RPC, such transactions can no longer be decoded. From P2P, a transaction
or block containing one is ignored like other malformed messages, rather
than rejected by validation.

p2p: reject transactions without inputs or outputs when deserializing

Add a reject_empty flag to TransactionSerParams, which makes
deserialization fail as soon as a transaction is found to have no
inputs or no outputs. Such transactions are never valid, but are
currently fully deserialized (along with the rest of the message) before
validation rejects them.

This reduces the memory a peer can make us allocate by sending a block
full of such transactions. At 10 bytes each, about 400000 of them fit in
a block message, each of which gets its own CTransaction. With this
change, the smallest transaction that gets deserialized has one input
and one output, which takes 60 bytes.

The flag is enabled (as TX_WITH_WITNESS_P2P) only where transactions are
received from P2P peers: tx and block messages, and the transactions in
cmpctblock and blocktxn messages. Like other malformed messages, these
are now ignored, rather than, for a block, causing the peer to be
disconnected, or, for a transaction, being added to the reject filters.
The functional tests are updated accordingly.

I have dropped all but the first two commits; I think it's fair that the performance gains don't justify the complexity being added here.

FWIW, here are the benchmarks (Zen5, gcc 15.3 x86_64, median of 11 runs each) I'm basing that on, in milliseconds, with this PR's (former version) on top of #36918. The "+counts" and "+empty" commits remain; the "+weight" one is dropped now.

| block | master | #36918  | +counts | +empty | +weight |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| ❌ 399,700 txs, 0 txins/txouts | 108 | 108 | 109 | 0.001 | 0.001 |
| ❌ no outputs, witness 2.0M × 1 B | 126 | 15 | 15 | 0.001 | 0.001 |
| ❌ 1 tx with 97,487 inputs | 8.0 | 3.7 | 0.001 | 0.001 | 0.001 |
| ❌ 1 tx with 444,111 outputs | 22 | 22 | 0.001 | 0.001 | 0.001 |
| ❌ 66,616 txs of 60 B | 28 | 27 | 27 | 27 | 4.1 |
| ❌ 4 txs with 24,300 inputs each | 5.1 | 4.8 | 5.4 | 5.3 | 1.0 |
| ❌ 1.05 MB scriptSig, witness 1.45M × 1 B | 57 | 12 | 12 | 12 | 0.02 |
| ❌ 1,055 WU, witness 2.0M × 1 B | 138 | 15 | 15 | 15 | 13 |

ACK 82cd7e742729bdfd5ea3be9c029c63ee9ad1f59d

Makes sense to keep just these two commits and leave peer disconnect handling for undeserializable messages to a follow-up. Checked the `num_inputs == 0` cases in `UnserializeTransaction` and the P2P call sites, and ran the updated unit and functional tests locally.

ACK 82cd7e742729bdfd5ea3be9c029c63ee9ad1f59d

I’m glad you dropped the weight accounting and stream state - I was uneasy about touching that much serialization code for this, and the two remaining checks are much easier to review. I also prefer `reserve` with `emplace_back` here, filling each entry just after construction seems cache-friendlier - and it was slightly faster when I timed block decoding locally.

I’d give the decoder some room above the block-derived counts so a transaction with one extra input still gets the usual validation error - to be on the safe side, since we only want to reject very obviously wrong entries.
I’d also find the minimum input weight easier to check if it used the field widths directly in place of `36 + 1 + 4`. The output bound could also be shared with `AccessByTxid`. If we keep the tight caps, I’d lean toward a release note for RPC and kernel callers. With limits that only catch obviously excessive counts, I’d skip it.

`UnserializeTransaction` is the part I’d be most careful about changing again: I need the same parsing order in #36548 and would like to share it if there’s a small extraction we’re comfortable with.
I’d also find `end of data` clearer than `Superfluous witness record` when [the outputs are cut off](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36906#discussion_r4697816420).

Done.

My concern is/was mostly with something like a change `READWRITE(block.vtx);` into `READWRITE(TX_WITH_WITNESS(block.vtx));`, which would introduce a new scope without limiting, or a scope with limiting but a different variable (this exact example might not work, but you see what I mean).

I've switched to your approach, but added a feature for parameters to declare they cannot be overridden, which would satisfy that concern and doesn't cause any compilation problems.

Can this stall block download when a requested block fails deserialization?

If an oversized block throws `std::ios_base::failure` in `vRecv >> TX_WITH_WITNESS_P2P`, the exception unwinds out of `ProcessMessage` before `RemoveBlockRequest(hash, pfrom.GetId())` runs. Since the peer isn't disconnected, the hash stays in `mapBlocksInFlight` until the 10-minute download timeout expires.

That's a fair concern. It's no different from how we treat a peer that never responds to a `getdata` requests at all, but extending the definition of serialization-invalid means that there are potentially broken (but not malicious) peers out there that aren't disconnected quickly anymore.

I'll investigate (separate from this PR) whether we can just blanket disconnect any peers that gives us undeserializable messages.

> [82cd7e7](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36906/changes/82cd7e742729bdfd5ea3be9c029c63ee9ad1f59d) _p2p: reject transactions without inputs or outputs when deserializing_:

This also changes what RPC and kernel callers can inspect. A short release note with the two counts would help explain why a transaction that used to decode now fails.

<details>
<summary>Document transaction decoding changes for callers</summary>

```patch
diff --git a/doc/release-notes-36906.md b/doc/release-notes-36906.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..3fd3e5c8bd
--- /dev/null
+++ b/doc/release-notes-36906.md
@@ -0,0 +1,20 @@
+P2P and network changes
+-----------------------
+
+- The node ignores `tx`, `block`, `cmpctblock` and `blocktxn` messages that
+  contain a transaction with no inputs or no outputs, or with more inputs
+  or outputs than can fit in a block.
+
+Updated RPCs
+------------
+
+- RPC decoding now rejects a transaction declaring more than 24,390 inputs
+  or 111,111 outputs. Either count alone exceeds the block weight limit.
+  With `iswitness` omitted, `decoderawtransaction` can still return a
+  different transaction if the same bytes decode in legacy format.
+
+Low-level changes
+=================
+
+- The same count limits apply to `btck_transaction_create` and
+  `btck_block_create`, which return null on decode failure.
```

</details>

> [82cd7e7](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36906/changes/82cd7e742729bdfd5ea3be9c029c63ee9ad1f59d) _p2p: reject transactions without inputs or outputs when deserializing_:

Getting `Superfluous witness record` when the output data is incomplete could be confusing for the user, we could also check `flags` here...

<details>
<summary>Preserve output-count parsing for zero-input transactions</summary>

```patch
diff --git a/src/primitives/transaction.h b/src/primitives/transaction.h
index a4be11ca43..88a3161099 100644
--- a/src/primitives/transaction.h
+++ b/src/primitives/transaction.h
@@ -241,5 +241,4 @@ void UnserializeTransaction(TxType& tx, Stream& s, const TransactionSerParams& p
 
-    // Read the number of outputs. In case of an empty vin, the byte read as the flags is the number of outputs (if the
-    // flags are not zero, there is witness data without inputs, which fails below).
-    auto num_outputs = (num_inputs == 0 && fAllowWitness) ? uint64_t{0} : ReadCompactSize(s);
+    // Read the number of outputs unless we already read the zero output count as the flags byte.
+    auto num_outputs = (num_inputs == 0 && fAllowWitness && flags == 0) ? uint64_t{0} : ReadCompactSize(s);
     if (num_outputs > MAX_BLOCK_WEIGHT / MIN_WEIGHT_PER_TXOUT) throw std::ios_base::failure("Too many transaction outputs");
diff --git a/src/test/transaction_tests.cpp b/src/test/transaction_tests.cpp
index a4ef16bd9e..63932b3e08 100644
--- a/src/test/transaction_tests.cpp
+++ b/src/test/transaction_tests.cpp
@@ -1501,4 +1501,7 @@ BOOST_AUTO_TEST_CASE(reject_empty)
     BOOST_CHECK_EXCEPTION(deser_tx(ext_no_inputs, TX_WITH_WITNESS_P2P), std::ios_base::failure, HasReason("Transaction without inputs"));
-    // ... even when the outputs that would follow are missing.
+    // Ordinary decoding reports the truncated output or its missing count.
+    ext_no_inputs.resize(9);
+    BOOST_CHECK_EXCEPTION(deser_tx(ext_no_inputs, TX_WITH_WITNESS), std::ios_base::failure, HasReason("end of data"));
     ext_no_inputs.resize(7);
+    BOOST_CHECK_EXCEPTION(deser_tx(ext_no_inputs, TX_WITH_WITNESS), std::ios_base::failure, HasReason("end of data"));
     BOOST_CHECK_EXCEPTION(deser_tx(ext_no_inputs, TX_WITH_WITNESS_P2P), std::ios_base::failure, HasReason("Transaction without inputs"));
```

</details>

comments.body:
> [ec2cabb](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36906/changes/ec2cabb795b616ac39b9e62df60bd9ed3ffa5af2) _primitives: reject txs with more inputs or outputs than fit in a block_:

I’d leave some room above the consensus limits - given this is meant to avoid extremes.
For the one extra input in this test I’d still expect `bad-txns-oversize` from validation.
A separate case farther over the limit could check for `TX decode failed`.

> [ec2cabb](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36906/changes/ec2cabb795b616ac39b9e62df60bd9ed3ffa5af2) _primitives: reject txs with more inputs or outputs than fit in a block_:

Following up on [my review of #36521](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36521#pullrequestreview-5871920324) now that the count checks are here. I need the same parsing order in #36548 to strip witnesses without building transactions. Would it make sense to extract the common part here so we only have one place to update these rules? I tried that with [lambdas for the input, output and witness reads](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36548/changes/e7976647484f3a3a5e5c964c30265a6e402eab81#diff-32f83e93b123235079fbadc3f68f8158c56c67d031a579475e16c6857edbecbfR189-R219) - but maybe that's too much and there's a safer or simpler way.
I also did a reindex-chainstate which showed no speed difference whatsoever.

> [ec2cabb](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36906/changes/ec2cabb795b616ac39b9e62df60bd9ed3ffa5af2) _primitives: reject txs with more inputs or outputs than fit in a block_:

I’d find these minimum weights easier to check if the expressions named the fields. `Txid::size() + sizeof(COutPoint::n)` shows where the 36 comes from, and `GetSizeOfCompactSize(0)` gives the empty script’s length prefix in both cases.

<details>
<summary>Use the serialized field widths for the minimum transaction weights</summary>

```patch
diff --git a/src/primitives/transaction.h b/src/primitives/transaction.h
index a7136281a9..ade6989299 100644
--- a/src/primitives/transaction.h
+++ b/src/primitives/transaction.h
@@ -184,6 +184,6 @@ inline constexpr TransactionSerParams TX_NO_WITNESS{.allow_witness = false};
 
-/** The minimum weight of a transaction input: its prevout (36 bytes), an empty scriptSig (1), and its nSequence (4). */
-inline constexpr uint64_t MIN_WEIGHT_PER_TXIN{WITNESS_SCALE_FACTOR * (36 + 1 + 4)};
-/** The minimum weight of a transaction output: its nValue (8 bytes) and an empty scriptPubKey (1). */
-inline constexpr uint64_t MIN_WEIGHT_PER_TXOUT{WITNESS_SCALE_FACTOR * (8 + 1)};
+/** Minimum input weight with an empty scriptSig. */
+inline constexpr uint64_t MIN_WEIGHT_PER_TXIN{WITNESS_SCALE_FACTOR * (Txid::size() + sizeof(COutPoint::n) + GetSizeOfCompactSize(0) + sizeof(CTxIn::nSequence))};
+/** Minimum output weight with an empty scriptPubKey. */
+inline constexpr uint64_t MIN_WEIGHT_PER_TXOUT{WITNESS_SCALE_FACTOR * (sizeof(CTxOut::nValue) + GetSizeOfCompactSize(0))};
 
```

</details>
